dse_runs.notes: Hard error constraint: max_abs_err <= 2^-20 (9.5367e-07) — this is a precision-dominated spec, so accuracy, not speed, is the binding constraint. Prioritise data_width and iteration/unroll depth large enough to reach ~20+ bits of accuracy (truncation/rounding error scales ~2^-width, CORDIC angle-quantisation error ~2^-n_iter): the exhaustive frontier almost certainly sits at high data_width (>= 24-28) and high n_iter (>= 20-24); low-width/low-iteration designs will be infeasible. Throughput >= 50 MSPS only needs to be met, not beaten, so for the min-luts_plus_ffs selection the cheapest way to reach 50 MSPS at high n_iter is likely a well-pipelined/unrolled-but-modest-parallelism structure or a multi-cycle iterative variant with a fast enough clock — do NOT buy throughput with area beyond the 50 MSPS requirement. Cover the full registry range in the searches, concentrate evals where the error constraint is feasible, and make sure the reported front has dense coverage along the area/power trade-off among feasible designs. Also return the L2 shortlist covering the smallest-area feasible designs.

final_text: The single queued spec, **high_precision**, is finalized. I spent its full 400-evaluation L1 budget on the structured DSE graph (`run_dse`, 400/400 used, inner architect stopping after three map_front rounds), which returned one feasible non-dominated front design; the search was steered toward the binding precision constraint (error ≤ 2^-20 needs high width/iteration count) while treating the ≥50 MSPS throughput as a floor to meet rather than beat, since the selection rule is min luts_plus_ffs. The L2 simulation found no system scenario for this spec but still supplied recorded facts (6-cycle contract latency, 1 input/cycle, simulated DDS SFDR 141.8 dBc / SNR 130.7 dB) and left the selection unchanged. Down-ladder, L3 `verify_rtl` had no recorded row for this configuration and a fresh exhaustive W=26 run was too heavy for a live campaign, L4 `synthesize` had no recorded synthesis (L4 is never run live), and L5 `back_annotate` returned `no_measured_data` — nothing to compare against the estimates — so no WINNER CHANGE was flagged and `reexplore` was correctly not invoked. The finalized selection is `pipelined_m:data_width=26,n_iter=22,angle_guard=4,frac_guard=0,rounding=round,m=7` with **luts_plus_ffs = 2364** (1953 LUTs + 412 FFs, calibrated cost-model estimate), **power_index = 4.45**, **throughput = 52 MSPS** (constraint met), and **max_abs_err = 6.47e-07 = 2^-20.56** (exact golden model, a 1.47× margin under the 2^-20 limit) — the smallest-area feasible, in-spec point returned by the Pareto search.
